# Proverbs 17 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** Better [is] a-morsel dry and-quietness with-it, than-a-house full-of sacrifices-of strife.

**2** A-servant [who]-acts-wisely will-rule over-a-son [who]-acts-shamefully, and-in-[the]-midst-of brothers he-will-share [the]-inheritance.

**3** A-refining-pot for-silver and-a-furnace for-gold, but-[the]-one-testing hearts [is] YHWH.

**4** An-evildoer gives-heed to-lips-of iniquity; falsehood listens to-a-tongue-of destruction.

**5** One-mocking [the]-poor reproaches his-Maker; one-rejoicing at-calamity will-not-go-unpunished.

**6** Crown-of old-men [are the]-sons'-sons, and-[the]-glory-of sons [is] their-fathers.

**7** Not fitting for-a-fool [are]-lips-of excellence; how-much-less for-a-noble [are]-lips-of falsehood.

**8** A-stone-of grace [is] the-bribe in-[the]-eyes-of its-possessor; everywhere it-turns it-prospers.

**9** One-covering a-transgression seeks love, but-one-repeating a-matter separates a-close-friend.

**10** A-rebuke goes-deeper into-[the]-discerning than-striking a-fool a-hundred-[times].

**11** Only rebellion a-bad-[person] seeks, and-a-messenger cruel will-be-sent against-him.

**12** Let-a-bear bereaved meet a-man, and-not a-fool in-his-folly.

**13** One-returning evil for-good — evil will-not-depart from-his-house.

**14** [The]-beginning-of strife [is] releasing water; so-before strife breaks-out, abandon [it].

**15** One-justifying [the]-wicked and-one-condemning [the]-righteous — an-abomination-of YHWH, even both-of-them.

**16** Why [is] this — a-price in-[the]-hand-of a-fool to-acquire wisdom, and-heart there-is-none?

**17** At-all-times the-friend loves, and-a-brother for-adversity is-born.

**18** A-man lacking heart strikes a-hand, becoming-surety before his-neighbor.

**19** One-loving transgression loves strife; one-making-high his-door seeks destruction.

**20** [The]-twisted-of heart does-not-find good, and-one-turned in-his-tongue falls into-evil.

**21** One-who-begets a-fool — for-grief to-him; and-not does-rejoice [the]-father-of a-fool.

**22** A-heart joyful does-good [as] medicine, but-a-spirit stricken dries-up [the]-bone.

**23** A-bribe from-[the]-bosom [the]-wicked takes, to-turn-aside paths-of justice.

**24** Before [the]-face-of [the]-discerning [is] wisdom, but-[the]-eyes-of a-fool [are] at-[the]-end-of [the]-earth.

**25** A-vexation to-his-father [is] a-son foolish, and-bitterness to-her-who-bore-him.

**26** Also to-fine [the]-righteous [is]-not good, to-strike nobles for-uprightness.

**27** One-restraining his-words knows knowledge, and-cool-of spirit [is] a-man-of understanding.

**28** Even a-fool keeping-silent is-considered wise; one-closing his-lips — discerning.

---
## EMET Literal Notes

- **17:3**: Matsref (crucible) and kur (furnace) — metallurgical testing as metaphor for divine examination of the inner person.

- **17:17**: Be-khol et — 'at all times.' The friend (re'a) and the brother (ach) together constitute the complete social safety net.

- **17:22**: Lev same'ach yetiv gehah — 'a heart joyful does good medicine.' One of the earliest statements connecting emotional state to physical health.

— EMET
